readme_description:
For a binary tree T, we can define a flip operation as follows: choose any node, and swap the left and right child subtrees.

A binary tree X is flip equivalent to a binary tree Y if and only if we can make X equal to Y after some number of flip operations.

Given the roots of two binary trees root1 and root2, return true if the two trees are flip equivalent or false otherwise.

list.content:
![Example 1](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2018/11/29/tree_ex.png)

```
Input: root1 = [1,2,3,4,5,6,null,null,null,7,8], root2 = [1,3,2,null,6,4,5,null,null,null,null,8,7]
Output: true
Explanation: We flipped at nodes with values 1, 3, and 5.
```

readme_constraints:
• The number of nodes in each tree is in the range [0, 100].
  • Each tree will have unique node values in the range [0, 99].
helpers_run_signature: (solution_class: type, root1_list: list[int | None], root2_list: list[int | None])
helpers_run_body:
root1 = TreeNode[int].from_list(root1_list)
    root2 = TreeNode[int].from_list(root2_list)
    implementation = solution_class()
    return implementation.flip_equiv(root1, root2)
